examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
model: opus  # default model
retries: 3
agents:
  coder: file:agents/coder.yaml

.troupe/agents/coder.yaml:
temperature: 0.2
tools: [shell, edit]
examples.input: `config get agents.coder.missing` (first command run against the theatre)

results.1: both arms: exit 5, 'path not found' on stderr; no file changed
results.2: all four arms: exit 5, 'not found' on stderr (wording differs; one arm prefixes the include file's path); no file changed

results.1: both arms: exit 3, refused because the value comes from the include agents/coder.yaml; no file changed
results.2: all four arms: exit 3, same refusal (wording differs; some say to change the included file instead); no file changed

results.1: both arms: exit 2, 'TROUPE_ACTOR must be human:<id> or agent:<id>'; nothing printed on stdout
results.2: all four arms: exit 2, same complaint in different words; nothing printed on stdout

results.1:
both arms: exit 0; .troupe/troupe.yml now reads:
model: sonnet # default model
retries: 3
agents:
  coder: file:agents/coder.yaml
results.2:
all four arms: exit 0; .troupe/troupe.yml now reads:
model: sonnet # default model
retries: 3
agents:
  coder: file:agents/coder.yaml

results.1: both arms: exit 0; 6 entries: seq 1-5 are one import (model=opus, retries=3, agents.coder.temperature=0.2, agents.coder.tools.0=shell, agents.coder.tools.1=edit; actor unknown, via import), then seq 6 is the set model opus→sonnet by human:owner with the reason
results.2: all four arms: exit 0; the same 6 entries: one import (seq 1-5), then the set (seq 6)

context.in_practice: In this run every arm on both routes behaved the same. Exactly one import was recorded, before the successful set, and it was never repeated or lost. The earlier failures (exits 5, 3, 2) did not wipe it out or cause a second import. The history doesn't show which earlier command triggered the import, so this run can't tell 'first command of any kind' apart from 'first command whose configuration loads'.
context.stakes: A user's first few commands against a theatre may fail (missing key, refused write, bad TROUPE_ACTOR). What matters is whether the history still begins with one clean import of the original file, or whether a failure loses or duplicates it.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 leaves open what happens to the import after a failure. Route 2 pins it down (the import stands after exits 2, 3 or 5; a load failure records nothing), but this run showed no visible difference between them.

plan_why: The theatre's first three commands all fail (exit 5 on a missing path, exit 3 on replacing a whole include, exit 2 on a bad TROUPE_ACTOR). Then a successful set runs, and history shows whether the import events exist, which command their timestamp and change id belong to, and that each appears only once. Caveat: if a route throws the import away and the next command redoes it, history may look the same, so timestamps and change ids may be the only visible difference. A load failure (exit 4) that leaves no record cannot be shown, because files cannot be fixed between commands.
routes: The first command against a theatre imports it (persistence after a later failure not stated)
The first command whose configuration loads imports it; the import stands even if that command then exits 2, 3 or 5; a load failure records nothing
